etymologies.etymologyHTML: From over- +‎ eat.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To eat too much of.

quote.citation: 2019, Alberto Villoldo, Grow a New Body, page 66:
quote.text: Overeat meat and you will not be flipping the genetic switches to grow a new body; instead, you will be opting for an early death even as you tone and strengthen your muscles.

definitions.definition: (reflexive, dated) To surfeit with eating. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1828, JT Smith, Nollekens and His Times, Century Hutchinson, published 1986, page 255:
quote.text: Mr. Nollekens, when he dined out of late years, always over-ate himself, particularly with the pastry and dessert.

quote.citation: 1896, The Eclectic Magazine of Foreign Literature, Science, and Art:
quote.text: At breakfast they overate themselves with buttered toast, and "had eaten so much that they could not learn with any pleasure,"  […]
